dek: Amber Fort, on a ridge above Maota Lake, was the seat of the Kachhwaha rulers before they moved to Jaipur, and is one of Rajasthan's finest palace-forts.

hero.alt: The garden courtyard and Jai Mandir palace inside Amber Fort, near Jaipur

intro: Amber (Amer) was the capital of the Kachhwaha Rajputs until Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur in 1727. The palace-fort seen today was commissioned by Raja Man Singh I, a general at Akbar's court, in 1592, and expanded by later rulers including Mirza Raja Jai Singh I. It blends Rajput and Mughal design in pale yellow sandstone and white marble.

The fort sits about 11 km north of Jaipur, above Maota Lake, and is linked by walls and passages to Jaigarh Fort on the ridge above. Amber is one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.
quickAnswer: Amber (Amer) Fort is about 11 km from central Jaipur and is part of the UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan. Commissioned by Raja Man Singh I in 1592, it includes the Diwan-i-Aam, Ganesh Pol, the mirrored Sheesh Mahal and the zenana. Walk up from the road or take a jeep; allow two to three hours, and combine it with Jaigarh and Nahargarh forts. October to March is the best time.
takeaways: Amber is about 11 km north of central Jaipur.
It is one of the six UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan.
The Sheesh Mahal, Ganesh Pol and Diwan-i-Aam are the highlights.
Arrive at opening time to beat tour groups and the heat.
Jaigarh and Nahargarh forts on the same ridge make a full day.

sections.heading: Getting up the hill
list: On foot: a cobbled path from the road below takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
By jeep: shared or private jeeps run from the road to the upper gate.
Elephant rides have been offered up the hill; welfare concerns have been widely raised, and many visitors now choose to walk or take a jeep.

sections.heading: Visiting practicalities
list: Open daily from morning to early evening; a light and sound show has run in the evenings.
Tickets at the fort or through Rajasthan's official ticketing; composite tickets have covered several Jaipur monuments.
Allow two to three hours, and hire a licensed guide at the official counter if you want the history.
Arrive at opening time; mid-morning brings the largest groups.

items.name: Jaigarh and Nahargarh
body: Jaigarh, above Amber, has ramparts and a large old cannon; Nahargarh overlooks Jaipur, best at sunset.

items.name: Jaipur city
body: City Palace, Jantar Mantar and the Hawa Mahal in the UNESCO-listed walled city.

sections.heading: A short history
paras: Amber was the Kachhwaha capital from the 11th century, long before the present palace. Raja Man Singh I, one of Akbar's leading generals, began the palace-fort in 1592, and it grew under his successors, especially Mirza Raja Jai Singh I in the 17th century. When Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur in 1727, the court moved to the plains, and Amber became a ceremonial and religious centre, with the Shila Devi temple inside the fort still in worship.

sections.heading: Best time and a suggested day

rows: Amber Fort, including the Sheesh Mahal
Lunch, then the Jal Mahal viewpoint by Man Sagar

after: October to March is best. The monsoon turns the hills green; summer afternoons are very hot.

safety: Timings, closures and ticket rules are set by the ASI, state archaeology departments or site trusts and change from time to time; check the official website before you go.
Do not climb on or touch carvings, and follow the site's rules on photography, drones and tripods.
Carry water and a hat; many sites have little shade, and Indian summers are hot.
Hold the railings on steep stairs and uneven ramparts.
packing: Comfortable shoes for cobbles and stairs

faqs.q: How far is Amber Fort from Jaipur?
faqs.a: About 11 km from the city centre, around 30 minutes by road.

faqs.q: Is Amber Fort a UNESCO site?
